name: Iniva (Institute of International Visual Arts)
funding: Arts Council England National Portfolio, Stuart Hall Foundation, charitable grants; registered educational charity.
watch: Founded in 1994 with Stuart Hall as founding chair. Holds the Stuart Hall Library on diaspora and global art.

name: Institute of Contemporary Art Indian Ocean (ICAIO)
funding: Founded in 2015 by Salim Currimjee, a painter, architect and collector.
watch: Exhibitions change each quarter, showing Mauritian, Indian and South African artists, at 51 Sir Seewoosagur Ramgoolam Street, Port Louis.
records_note: icaio.org now redirects to an unrelated gambling site, so ICAIO's own pages could not be read.

name: Instituto Inhotim
funding: R$ 60M budget. Federal Culture Incentive Law (Lei Rouanet), Vale Cultural Institute civic environmental agreements, and ticket revenues.
watch: Vale, whose 2019 dam collapse killed 270 nearby, pays the operating budget.
why_flagged: Vale, whose 2019 dam collapse killed 270 nearby, pays the operating budget.
records_note: Inhotim posts institutional reports from 2012 to 2025, audited financial statements for most years, sponsor logos by tier with no date, and its full council.

name: Instituto Tomie Ohtake
funding: Nubank (R$10M a year to 2027, about 40% of budget), Bradesco, Motiva, Instituto Votorantim, Bloomberg, Usiminas and others. 98% of funds come through the Rouanet tax law; free entry.
watch: Bloomberg Philanthropies faces a May 2026 UK artists' letter to five London theatres over Israel; no action is aimed at Tomie Ohtake.
records_note: Posts balance sheets for 2023 and 2024 and names its three governing bodies; sponsors appear as tiered logos with no date, and no annual report.

name: International Center of Photography
funding: About $8M revenue and $15M expenses (FY2023 Form 990); corporate supporters are Fondation d'entreprise Hermès, Select Equity, Harlowe, Paramount Global, MPB and Hearst.
watch: 2020 open letter from about 150 community members over students' protest photos; ICP refused to make students take them down.
records_note: Form 990s for 2021 to 2024 are posted on its site and in ProPublica; corporate supporters show as undated logos, and the board is listed.

name: Inverleith House (Royal Botanic Garden)
funding: £0.8M art program. Scottish Government environment directorate, Outset, Paul Mellon Centre.

name: IZOLYATSIA
funding: Non-profit platform founded in 2010 in Donetsk. After 2014 most money came from unnamed international, EU and US grants. Creative Europe co-funds ZMINA with Trans Europe Halles and Malý Berlín.
watch: Russian-backed forces seized its Donetsk site in 2014 and run a prison there. It moved to Kyiv. Only 2011 and 2012 annual reports are posted.
records_note: IZOLYATSIA posts only 2011 and 2012 reports; it publishes no accounts, named funders or board.

name: Jakarta Biennale
funding: Run since 2024 by Majelis Jakarta, an artist-collective network. 2026 partners: Dulux, Artotel's Paviliun Raden Saleh, iForte. Jakarta culture office and Jakpro logos are unlabelled; no budget published.
watch: Founded 1974 by the Jakarta Arts Council. The 2026 edition, KEBAL, runs 4 Oct to 28 Nov at Taman Ismail Marzuki.
records_note: The partner page shows sponsor and media-partner logos with role labels only; no reports, accounts, dates or board are published.

name: Japan Folk Crafts Museum (Nihon Mingeikan)
funding: 2025: public-interest foundation chaired by Naoto Fukasawa, run on admissions, members' dues (corporate from JPY 100k) and donations; no roster published.
watch: Founded 1936 by Yanagi Soetsu with backing from industrialist Ohara Magosaburo; supporting members are not named.
records_note: The foundation posts yearly business reports for FY2018 to FY2025, income and expenditure statements and its officer list, but no donor roster.

name: Jeu de Paume
funding: €8.6M budget in 2024, 68% from the Ministry of Culture; Jaeger-LeCoultre, CHANEL, Fondation Neuflize OBC, Louis Roederer and Swiss Life also fund it.
watch: 2013 censorship row: after a complaint from the CRIF, the culture ministry made it add visitor notices to Ahlam Shibli's show.
records_note: Activity reports 2019 to 2025 are posted, but without financial statements; the patrons page shows undated logos, and the governance page lists the association's members.

name: John Hansard Gallery
funding: University of Southampton, Arts Council England National Portfolio, Southampton City Council; public university gallery.

name: Jüdisches Museum Berlin
funding: Federal Government Commissioner for Culture and the Media (BKM) public budget.
